output.entity_proposed: Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) Council
output.proposal: HB No. 9425 seeks to mandate the formulation of a thirty-year Comprehensive Infrastructure Development Masterplan (CIDMP) and to establish the Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) Council to lead its preparation and revision, in order to institutionalize long-term infrastructure planning and ensure policy continuity across administrations.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the MIND Council's mandate to formulate, coordinate and monitor the CIDMP relates to the planning, programming and monitoring roles already performed by the Department of Economy, Planning and Development (DEPDev), which the bill also designates as lead coordinator and Secretariat under Section 6 (Infrastructure Policies and Strategies) and Section 11 (Secretariat to the MIND Council), and whether a new inter-agency council is consistent with the streamlining and reduction of overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The measure aligns with the Infrastructure Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on the timely completion of flagship and high-impact infrastructure, climate-resilient design and public-private partnerships. It corresponds to item 34 of the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda (Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development).
legislative_history: HB No. 9425 was filed on May 26, 2026 by Representative Jeffrey Soriano; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available records.
HB No. 11371 (20th Congress) carries near-identical provisions, differing mainly in the number of industry stakeholder members of the Council (five instead of four).
HB No. 3959 (filed August 26, 2025) and HB No. 4194 (filed September 1, 2025), both pending in committee in the 20th Congress, bear the same title; their texts have not been reviewed.
In the Senate, SB No. 2 (filed July 2, 2025) and SB No. 863 (filed August 4, 2025), both pending in committee, are titled the MIND Act.
In the 19th Congress, SB No. 2605, titled the MIND Act, reached the stage of Pending Second Reading, Special Order.

Earlier measures on a Comprehensive Infrastructure Development Master Plan without reference to the MIND Council include HB Nos. 1132 and 693 (20th Congress) and HB Nos. 8060, 8106 and 6343 and SB Nos. 158 and 1987 (19th Congress); SB Nos. 158 and 1987 were consolidated or substituted in a committee report.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 9425 seeks to institutionalize a thirty-year Comprehensive Infrastructure Development Masterplan (CIDMP) and to establish the Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) Council to lead its preparation and revision. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 5 (Formulation of a Comprehensive Infrastructure Development Master Plan) provides for a thirty-year CIDMP setting the country's long-term infrastructure vision, goals and strategy, to be reviewed and updated every ten years or earlier as needed, through a whole-of-government approach.
b. Section 6 (Infrastructure Policies and Strategies) provides the policies the CIDMP shall pursue, with DEPDev as lead coordinator, including prioritization principles, harmonization of national and local goals, public consultation and private sector participation.
c. Section 7 (Contents of the CIDMP) provides that the CIDMP shall contain a long-term vision, economic and demographic projections, sub-sector strategies, and indicative projects with timelines, estimated funding requirements and financing modalities.
d. Section 8 (Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) Council) establishes the Council to lead the preparation and revision of the CIDMP and requires DEPDev to mainstream the CIDMP in the planning-programming-budgeting documents, including the National Expenditure Program and the General Appropriations Act.
e. Section 9 (Composition of the MIND Council) provides that the Council shall be chaired by the President, with the DEPDev Secretary as Vice Chairperson, and shall include twelve other department secretaries, including the DBM Secretary, the presidents of the LGU Leagues, and four industry stakeholders selected under criteria set by the Council.
f. Section 10 (Powers and Functions of the MIND Council) provides that the Council shall formulate the CIDMP, coordinate infrastructure investments, monitor implementation, review and streamline existing policies, consult stakeholders, report and recommend legislation to Congress, and may form a consultative and advisory committee.
g. Section 11 (Secretariat to the MIND Council) provides that DEPDev shall serve as Secretariat and shall be responsible for formulating the detailed CIDMP, its updating, and its monitoring and evaluation.
h. Section 12 (Role of Implementing Agencies) provides that implementing agencies in the covered sub-sectors shall prioritize and fast-track projects in accordance with the CIDMP and pursue sector-specific objectives.
i. Section 13 (Consideration of Approved National Infrastructure Projects) provides that infrastructure projects approved by DEPDev before the Act takes effect shall be given due consideration in the CIDMP.
j. Section 14 (Joint Congressional Oversight Committee (JCOC)) creates an oversight committee of six members from each chamber that shall hold hearings at least quarterly.
k. Section 15 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the current year's appropriations of the departments and agencies concerned, and continuing requirements shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
l. Section 16 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the Council shall issue the implementing rules within ninety days of the Act's approval.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 9425 may be considered alongside HB No. 11371, which carries near-identical provisions in the same Congress, HB Nos. 3959 and 4194, which bear the same title, and SB Nos. 2 and 863, the MIND Act measures pending in the Senate, as well as the 19th Congress SB No. 2605. The measure aligns with the Infrastructure Development priority of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework and corresponds to item 34 of the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda. The review should assess whether the MIND Council adds a distinct function to the planning and coordination roles that Section 6 (Infrastructure Policies and Strategies), Section 8 (Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) Council) and Section 11 (Secretariat to the MIND Council) already assign to DEPDev, consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), and the implications of Section 8 for the budget preparation documents, including the National Expenditure Program and the General Appropriations Act.
